answer.reason: The old harness initializes Adam7 row state before calling png_set_interlace_handling. Row counts depend on the interlace bit at initialization, but the packet omits the setter’s behavior and the effective interlacing configuration. The subsequent duplicate-initialization report may also prevent execution from reaching the row loop. The frozen row-state consequence is therefore unproved.

scope_contract.reason: Sequential Adam7 row state belongs to the target’s PNG decoding operation.

feasible_trigger.reason: An Adam7 IHDR can select the relevant row-initialization condition, but the packet does not establish that this build supports interlacing or that the late setter and duplicate-call path permit an actual execution to reach the row loop.

evidence.quote:
# Disable logging via library build configuration control.
cat scripts/pnglibconf.dfa | \
  sed -e "s/option STDIO/option STDIO disabled/" \
      -e "s/option WARNING /option WARNING disabled/" \
      -e "s/option WRITE enables WRITE_INT_FUNCTIONS/option WRITE disabled/" \
> scripts/pnglibconf.dfa.temp
mv scripts/pnglibconf.dfa.temp scripts/pnglibconf.dfa

# build the library.
autoreconf -f -i
./configure
make -j$(nproc) clean
make -j$(nproc) libpng16.la

# build libpng_read_fuzzer.
$CXX $CXXFLAGS -std=c++11 -I. \
     $SRC/libpng/contrib/oss-fuzz/libpng_read_fuzzer.cc \
     -o $OUT/libpng_read_fuzzer \
     -lFuzzingEngine .libs/libpng16.a -lz

observable_consequence.reason: Row initialization chooses a pass row count from the current interlace bit, while the harness loops over full image height. Whether the late setter leaves that count inconsistent during png_read_row is unresolved; png_start_read_image can report duplicate initialization first.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: The harness does not use png_read_image’s late-setup repair or a pass-specific row loop. The omitted setter might itself reconcile initialized state, so an equivalent route cannot be excluded.

identity_preserved.reason: The same late-interlace-setup tuple is assessed against the same old harness in both source versions; this establishes identity, not whether either version has the claimed blocker.
